definitions.explanation: To capture someone's attention or interest; to make something appealing.

definitions.gloss: to pull toward oneself, to draw close
definitions.explanation: To physically pull something or someone closer.
When a body part (especially in children) has a convulsion or spasm. Often used in the form {引|ひ}き{付|つ}けを{起|お}こす.

examples.japanese: {注目|ちゅうもく}を{引|ひ}き{付|つ}ける。
その{映画|えいが}は{多|おお}くの{観客|かんきゃく}を{引|ひ}き{付|つ}けた。
examples.english: That movie attracted a large audience.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{話|はなし}し{方|かた}は{人|ひと}を{引|ひ}き{付|つ}ける{魅力|みりょく}がある。
examples.english: Her way of speaking has the charm to attract people.

examples.japanese: {椅子|いす}を{引|ひ}き{付|つ}けて{座|すわ}った。
examples.english: I pulled the chair closer and sat down.

examples.japanese: テーブルを{壁|かべ}に{引|ひ}き{付|つ}けて{置|お}いた。
examples.english: I placed the table pulled up against the wall.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもを{引|ひ}き{付|つ}けて{抱|だ}きしめた。
examples.english: I drew the child close and hugged them.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんが{高熱|こうねつ}で{引|ひ}き{付|つ}けを{起|お}こした。
examples.english: The baby had a convulsion due to high fever.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{引|ひ}き{付|つ}けを{起|お}こしたら、すぐに{病院|びょういん}に{連|つ}れて{行|い}ってください。
examples.english: If a child has a convulsion, take them to the hospital immediately.

examples.japanese: {熱性|ねっせい}けいれんで{引|ひ}き{付|つ}けを{起|お}こすことがある。
examples.english: Febrile seizures can sometimes cause convulsions.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive).

COMPOUND VERB: Formed from {引|ひ}く (to pull) + {付|つ}ける (to attach). The combination creates the meaning of 'pulling something toward and attaching it' or figuratively 'drawing attention.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{注目|ちゅうもく}を{引|ひ}き{付|つ}ける (attract attention)
・{興味|きょうみ}を{引|ひ}き{付|つ}ける (draw interest)
・{人|ひと}を{引|ひ}き{付|つ}ける (attract people)
・{引|ひ}き{付|つ}けを{起|お}こす (have a convulsion)

SIMILAR WORDS: {魅了|みりょう}する is more literary for 'to captivate.'
